title: craftos-mcp world
description: A world file: `<name>.world.json` next to a program, or `worlds/<name>.json`. The world itself, plus the monitor walls the window, the VS Code extension and the test runner attach from it. schemas/world.schema.json is generated from this type (world-schema.test.ts).

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of this file, for editors. The runner ignores it.

monitors.description: Monitor walls next to the computer (`craftos-mcp window`, the VS Code extension and `*.test.lua` runs).
monitors.markdownDescription: Monitor walls next to the computer (`craftos-mcp window`, the VS Code extension and `*.test.lua` runs).

addons.description: Mods besides CC:Tweaked this world has (addons.ts): addon ids such as "advanced-peripherals", "mekanism", "create", or "all" / "none". Default: the CRAFTOS_ADDONS environment variable, else all. A peripheral of an addon that is off is an error.

enumDescriptions: Every addon that has a release for the world's Minecraft version.

version.description: The Minecraft version the computer is on (versions.ts): "1.18.2" (CC:Tweaked 1.101.3), "1.20.1" or "1.21.1" (CC:Tweaked 1.121.0), or { mc, cc?, loader? }. Default: the CRAFTOS_VERSION environment variable, else 1.18.2. It picks the ROM, the engine's CC:Tweaked behaviour and the mod versions; an addon with no release for that Minecraft cannot be switched on.

cc.description: CC:Tweaked version; must be the one this Minecraft version has.

loader.description: Mod loader. Default: the version's first.

simProgram.description: Give the computer the emulator's `sim` shell program, so a person can change the world by typing (`sim join Alice`). Not CC:Tweaked's, so off unless a person drives the computer (`craftos-mcp window` and `app` turn it on).
simProgram.markdownDescription: Give the computer the emulator's `sim` shell program, so a person can change the world by typing (`sim join Alice`). Not CC:Tweaked's, so off unless a person drives the computer (`craftos-mcp window` and `app` turn it on).

craftosPcApis.description: Give programs CraftOS-PC's `periphemu`, `config` and `mounter` APIs, for code written for CraftOS-PC. CC:Tweaked has none of them, so they are off by default. When on they act as the game would: periphemu.create places the block in this world, live; config and mounter answer but change nothing (docs/coming-from-craftos-pc.md).

motd.description: Show the ROM's message of the day (the random tip under "CraftOS 1.8") at boot. Default false here, so captured screens are the same every run; CC:Tweaked's own default is true (docs/conformance/emulator-vs-real-deviations.md).

vhcctweaks.description: Which vhcctweaks (github.com/Akkiruk/vhcctweaks, a Vault Hunters server mod for Minecraft 1.18.2 only) the server runs: an opt-in addon. Default off (`false`), or "2.2.36" when world.addons, craftos.json's addons or CRAFTOS_ADDONS name `vhcctweaks` ("all" leaves it out). "2.2.36": linked ender modems, listDetailed/moveMany, inventory watches, spending allowances, money calls on the economy thread and the rest (docs/vhcctweaks.md). "2.2.35" opts out, for comparisons with measurements made before 2.2.36; such a computer takes no part in links. "2.2.37" is 2.2.36 plus the 2.2.37 API as the emulator models it from the mod's spec: getPlayerGearPower/getPlayerTemper/getPlayerReputation, getPlayerSkills/getPlayerStats, the hotbar and counted weapon in getPlayerEquipment, getLimits (statCaps too), vhcc.getUsage, moveMany's expectName and the Gear Score fields in item details, and on every inventory listContents/pushContents/moveMany `inner` (backpacks, shulker boxes and vault barrels in a slot) and identify. `false`: no vhcctweaks at all, as does a ROM without /rom/ccsim/vhcc.lua. The server is plain CC:Tweaked 1.101.3, Advanced Peripherals 0.7.31r and Mekanism on their own defaults: no ccvault, vhcc or lockdown, a plain ender modem, AP's hidden "$" chat channel, working sendFormatted* chat box methods, a 100 ms chat cooldown and real isSlimeChunk.

linkLatency.description: What a call to a vhcctweaks-linked computer's monitor (or any of its peripherals' computer-thread methods) costs, in ms of game time, as in game (about 30 ms). "fast" (or 0) answers at once. Inventory methods wait for the server tick either way. Default CRAFTOS_LINK_LATENCY, else 30.

Default true. `false` is an older one: getPlayerGearPower and getPlayerTemper answer "gear power not available" and "temper not available" for a player on this server, a saved Temper has no multipliers, and gear gets no Gear Score fields.

identifyAvailable.description: 2.2.37, emulator only: `false` is a server whose Vault Hunters cannot identify from a computer, so an inventory's identify gives "identify not available" once every other check passed. Default true.
identifyAvailable.markdownDescription: 2.2.37, emulator only: `false` is a server whose Vault Hunters cannot identify from a computer, so an inventory's identify gives "identify not available" once every other check passed. Default true.

economyDelayTicks.description: 2.2.36: server ticks the economy thread takes per money call (transfer, getPlayerBalance, getBalance of someone not online here). Default 0: the answer comes at the next timer. Raise it to hold calls open in a test.

internalErrors.description: 2.2.36 tests: ccvault function name -> how many calls answer `nil, "internal error"` (-1: every call).
internalErrors.markdownDescription: 2.2.36 tests: ccvault function name -> how many calls answer `nil, "internal error"` (-1: every call).

position.description: Where the computer stands. Default x 0, y 64, z 0 in the overworld.

label.markdownDescription: The computer's label: os.getComputerLabel, and what another computer's `computer_N` peripheral answers to getLabel.

modemLink.description: Set by the runner on a computer whose modems reach other computers through a relay.

deploy.description: Assemble the computer from workspace subfolders instead of copying the whole workspace, like an installer does. Each entry copies `from` (workspace-relative) into `to` (computer-relative, default the root). Later entries win.

to.description: Where on the computer it goes. Default: "" (the root).

peripherals.description: Blocks next to the computer or on its wired network: inventories, tanks, speakers, modems, drives and the addons' blocks. Each type takes its own fields (see world-peripherals.ts, PeripheralTypeMap).

moonPhase.description: 0 full moon .. 7 waxing gibbous. Not read: getMoonId always answers 0, as the real block does.

uuid.description: Player UUID. Default 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<index as 12 hex digits>.

online.description: Offline players can still be hosts or have balances. Default true.

gamemode.description: Game mode; CC: Androids passes over a creative or spectator player.

dimension.description: Dimension the player is in. Default "minecraft:overworld".

airSupply.description: Air left, in ticks (Advanced Peripherals 0.7.48r+ getPlayerPos). Default 300.

equipment.description: What the player wears and holds, read by 2.2.36's ccvault.getPlayerEquipment. Items as in chests.

onOtherServer.description: 2.2.36: online on another server of the network. The economy knows them (balances, vault level), but this server treats them as offline.

gearPower.description: 2.2.37: what the player's six combat slots score, read by ccvault.getPlayerGearPower. Vault Hunters' scorer is not modelled: the world gives the slot scores and the emulator works out the rest as the game does.

temper.description: 2.2.37: the player's Temper and Dust, read by ccvault.getPlayerTemper (and Gear Power's multipliers).

reputation.description: 2.2.37: reputation with each vault god, read by ccvault.getPlayerReputation. Each defaults to 0.

skills.description: 2.2.37: the player's skill trees, read by ccvault.getPlayerSkills (online, or from the saved profile). `false`: Vault Hunters cannot read them ("skills not available").

secondary.description: Secondary effect id (the primary again: level II). Default: none.

pages.description: The pages: plain text for a book and quill, JSON text components for a written book.

UpwBookSpec.description: A book on a lectern: "minecraft:writable_book" or "minecraft:written_book" (anything else is no book).

__book.description: The book's pages, title and author.

UpwConfig.description: UnlimitedPeripheralWorks config overrides (PeripheralWorksConfig), by the mod's setting names.

cooldownTreshholdLevel.description: Cooldowns at or below this many ms do not start.

itemStorageTransferLimit.description: Most items one item pedestal pushItems/pullItems moves.

stationaryUniversalScanMaxFreeRadius.description: Universal scanner: largest radius that costs nothing (a bigger one fails: a block has no fuel).

stationaryUniversalScanMaxCostRadius.description: Universal scanner: largest radius at all (its maxRadius).

stationaryUniversalScanExtraBlockCost.description: Universal scanner: fuel per block past the free radius.

UpwItemSpec.description: An item a UPW block starts with; `count` may be left out. Other fields reach getItemDetail as they are.

count.description: Stack size (a display pedestal and a jukebox hold one).

disc.description: The record in it (count is always 1). Default: none.

playing.description: false: the record is in but not playing. Default: true when there is a disc.

book.description: The book on it. Default: none.

UpwLightSpec.description: Block and sky light, as the ultimate sensor's `light` inspector reads them.

UpwPlayerSpec.description: A player the universal scanner sees (`upw.players`).

uuid.description: Player UUID. Default: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-0001<place as 8 hex digits>.

x.description: X coordinate. A player without x, y and z is never seen.

width.description: Width of the box the scan meets.

height.description: Height of the box the scan meets, from the feet.

UpwWorld.description: UnlimitedPeripheralWorks: what the ultimate sensor reads, the scanner's players and config (docs/unlimited-peripheral-works.md).

dayTime.description: Day time in ticks at boot.

daylightCycle.description: false: the day time stands still; otherwise it moves one a tick of the virtual clock.

VirtualPeripheralSpec.description: Peripherals implemented in Lua by the sim: inventories, playerDetector, chatBox.

name.description: Peripheral name: a side of the computer or a network name.

type.description: Inventories ("minecraft:chest", "minecraft:barrel", ...), "fluid_storage" tanks, "speaker" (what it plays is listed in the sim state; `craftos-mcp window` plays it out loud), or an Advanced Peripherals type: playerDetector, chatBox, energyDetector, redstoneIntegrator, nbtStorage, environmentDetector, meBridge, rsBridge, arController; or a Mekanism QIO block (see QioBlockSpec): qioDriveArray, qioDashboard, qioImporter, qioExporter, qioRedstoneAdapter; or "quantumEntangloporter" (EntangloporterSpec).

items.description: Inventories: slot (1-based) -> item. Storage bridges: a list of stacks `{ name, amount, displayName?, nbt?, tags?, craftable? }`.
items.markdownDescription: Inventories: slot (1-based) -> item. Storage bridges: a list of stacks `{ name, amount, displayName?, nbt?, tags?, craftable? }`.

canChangeItems.description: vhcctweaks 2.2.37: `false` is an inventory that does not let its slots be set or hands out copies: pushContents, inner moves and identify give "can't change items in this inventory"; listContents still works. Default true.
canChangeItems.markdownDescription: vhcctweaks 2.2.37: `false` is an inventory that does not let its slots be set or hands out copies: pushContents, inner moves and identify give "can't change items in this inventory"; listContents still works. Default true.

WindGeneratorSpecFields.description: Mekanism wind generator. Its `y` sets the height multiplier.

minY.description: Lowest Y of the height range.

maxY.description: Highest Y of the height range.

energy.description: Stored J.

energyOutput.description: Cable load, J/t (at most the generator's output).

formed.description: false: the block starts unformed (only the tile's own methods).

security.description: Security mode; setters fail unless PUBLIC.

owner.description: Owner: a player name or UUID the world knows, or a raw UUID.

powered.description: Redstone signal at the start (the mekSetRedstone command changes it).

WorldScannerSpecFields.description: Some Peripherals world scanner. getBlockAt is relative to its position. No extra fields.
